rfm_tuples.R: Based on this evaluation, our management has concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was not effective as of December 31, 2024, due to the material weaknesses identified below. ... (i) risk assessment process, (ii) insufficient documentation of operating effectiveness, (iii) ineffective IT general controls related to user access at Interparfums SA subsidiary.
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution: compare 'controls effective' language to prior FY2023 10-K (accession 0001753926-24-000405)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-27) explicitly stated: 'our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2023' with no material weaknesses. FY2024 10-K abruptly disclosed three material weaknesses, an adverse auditor attestation, and an undocumented control environment — including IT general controls at the French subsidiary that runs ~65% of revenue. This is a one-year cliff, not a deteriorating trend.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Year-over-year flip from 'effective' to three material weaknesses + adverse ICFR audit opinion is a forensic red flag, especially with the IT general-controls weakness localized to the European subsidiary that originates the majority of revenue. Suggests the controls were never as 'effective' as previously claimed, or there was a deliberate scope change tied to the new auditor's first audit.

rfm_tuples.R: Interparfums, Inc. is the subject of an informal investigation from the staff of the Enforcement Division of the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the 'SEC'), and we have responded to the SEC staff denying any wrongdoing. The issue is related to the alleged failure to disclose in our August 2023 proxy statement certain issues that our prior auditor, Mazars USA LLP, had in 2018 and 2020, which were rectified in 2023. ... At the present time we have not yet heard back from the SEC staff.
rfm_tuples.f: edgar_fts: check whether 'informal investigation' language existed in any prior IPAR 10-K/10-Q/DEF14A pre-2025
rfm_tuples.M_value: edgar_fts hits for '"informal investigation"' filtered to CIK 0000822663 (2020-01-01 -> cutoff 2025-05-15): 1 hit, exclusively the 2025-03-11 10-K. Prior 10-Ks (FY2019-FY2023) contain ZERO references. The disclosure is brand-new in this filing, even though management states the underlying SEC inquiry concerns alleged non-disclosures in the AUGUST 2023 proxy — meaning the investigation has been live for >12 months without prior disclosure in either the FY2023 10-K (Feb 2024) or the three FY2024 10-Qs.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B finding: the SEC inquiry concerns conduct in the August 2023 proxy, but IPAR did not disclose the existence of an SEC informal investigation in the FY2023 10-K (filed Feb 2024) or any intervening 10-Q. Disclosure first surfaces only when paired with the auditor change and material-weakness admission. The clustering of three separately serious disclosures into one filing strongly suggests previously withheld material information.

rfm_tuples.R: Forvis Mazars, LLP (PCAOB ID 686) ... We have served as the Company's auditor since 2024. ... Mazars USA LLP (PCAOB ID 339) ... the Company's auditor from 2004 to 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: auditor_change_tracker: identify auditor change and surrounding context (was it driven by Forvis Mazars merger vs. dismissal / disagreement)
rfm_tuples.M_value: IPAR replaced Mazars USA LLP (auditor 2004-2024, 20-year tenure) with Forvis Mazars LLP in 2024. While the brand 'Mazars' is preserved, the filing repeatedly frames this as a merger-driven succession (Forvis LLP + Mazars USA LLP combined). However, the change coincided with (a) FIRST-EVER material-weakness finding in 20+ years, (b) FIRST disclosure of SEC informal investigation specifically about Mazars USA's own historical issues, and (c) NT 10-K filed 2025-03-03 (late filing). The 2024 audit fee structure shows $0.3M to Mazars USA (Q1 2024 only) and $1.4M to Forvis Mazars (Q2/Q3/10-K), suggesting an in-year transition, not a clean year-start change.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Even framed as a benign 'merger' transition, the new auditor's first attestation produced an adverse ICFR opinion AND surfaced three material weaknesses that Mazars USA never flagged across 20 years. Either prior audits missed material control failures or the new firm applied materially stricter standards on its first audit — both consistent with prior under-disclosure.

rfm_tuples.R: We have built a portfolio of prestige brands, which include Boucheron, Coach, Jimmy Choo, Karl Lagerfeld, Kate Spade, Lacoste, Lanvin, Moncler, Montblanc, Rochas, and Van Cleef & Arpels ... fragrance product sales through our European based operations represented approximately 65% of net sales for the year ended December 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: revenue_concentration: extract brand-level concentration vs total net sales; check single-brand and top-3 brand exposure
rfm_tuples.M_value: Top brands as % of net sales (2024 / 2023 / 2022): Jimmy Choo 17/17/18; Montblanc 15/17/18; Coach 14/15/15; GUESS 12/12/12; Donna Karan/DKNY 7/7/3; Lacoste 6/0/0; Ferragamo 5/5/5. Top 3 brands = 46% of sales; top 7 'largest brands' = 76% of 2024 sales (vs 73% in 2023 and 71% in 2022 — concentration RISING). Macy's = 12% of net sales (sole >10% customer; no >10% customer existed in 2022).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Concentration is real and worsening. Jimmy Choo + Montblanc + Coach = 46% of revenue and ALL are licensed brands held under finite-term agreements. Combined with rising channel concentration (Macy's now 12%, up from <10% in 2022) and growing dependence on Macy's at the same time Macy's faces well-known department-store headwinds, the boring-staple framing is misleading.

rfm_tuples.R: BENACIN PHILIPPE (President of Interparfums Inc. and CEO of Interparfums SA) sold 25,000 shares on 2025-03-21 at ~$117.38 per share for $2.93M (open-market sale, Form 4 filed 2025-03-24, NOT under a 10b5-1 plan).
rfm_tuples.f: insider_vs_calendar / form4: insider sales clustered to capital/disclosure events; check 10b5-1 designation and timing relative to 10-K filing
rfm_tuples.M_value: The 10-K disclosing material weaknesses and the SEC informal investigation was filed on 2025-03-11. President Benacin (co-founder, day-to-day operator, and one of the two officers the company calls 'critical' to the business) sold $2,934,602 worth of stock 10 calendar days later (2025-03-21), explicitly NOT under a Rule 10b5-1 plan ('During the fourth quarter of 2024, no director or officer has adopted or terminated either any Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement'). Across the 540-day pre-cutoff window the insider tool found 20 sales totaling $11.1M; the post-10-K Benacin sale alone accounts for 26% of that total. The 10-K's 'Other Information' (Item 9B) and the surrounding 10b5-1 cybersecurity-style attestations confirm there was no rule-based predetermined trading plan covering the sale.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Highest-conviction Mode-B finding: the President of the European subsidiary (which is where the IT general-controls material weakness LIVES, and which originates ~65% of revenue) executed a discretionary $2.9M open-market sale 10 days after the company first disclosed (a) three material weaknesses, (b) an SEC informal investigation, and (c) a late 10-K filing (NT 10-K on 2025-03-03). Selling discretion + proximity + magnitude + insider's operational role over the weakness area is textbook 'asymmetric information' clustering.

rfm_tuples.R: NT 10-K notification of late filing filed 2025-03-03 (accession 0001753926-25-000389), eight calendar days before the actual 10-K (2025-03-11).
rfm_tuples.f: edgar.list_filings: compare to prior year on-time filing pattern
rfm_tuples.M_value: IPAR filed FY2019, FY2020, FY2021, FY2022, FY2023 10-Ks all on time (between Feb 27 and Mar 2). FY2024 is the FIRST late 10-K filing in the available history, requiring an NT 10-K filing. The 10-K then arrived only 8 days late — consistent with the auditor needing additional time to finalize material-weakness language and the adverse ICFR opinion.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Late filings in companies with prior multi-decade on-time records are a known precursor to control issues. Here the NT 10-K is the visible artifact of the audit running over because of the new auditor's adverse ICFR findings.

rfm_tuples.R: Despite the finding of these material weaknesses, we have concluded that our consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K fairly present in all material respects the financial condition, results of operations and cash flows of the Company ... we believe that these actions, collectively, will remediate the material weaknesses identified.
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution: check whether Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-05) reports any actual remediation progress versus plan
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-05, last pre-cutoff filing) reiterates verbatim that 'our material weaknesses will not be considered remediated until the controls operate for a sufficient period of time' and references the same Remediation Plan from the 10-K. No specific milestone met. No new control implemented. Plan still depends on engaging a third-party advisor. ~55 days after the 10-K disclosure, no measurable remediation has occurred.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The remediation language is a forward-looking 'plan to plan': the company commits to engaging a third party and will redesign user-access controls at Interparfums SA. As of the last pre-cutoff filing there has been no progress beyond restating the plan. Material weaknesses tied to French-subsidiary IT user access are not quickly cured.

rfm_tuples.R: In February 2024, our Board of Directors increased the annual dividend to $3.00 per share. In February 2025, our Board of Directors further increased the annual dividend to $3.20 per share. The next quarterly cash dividend of $0.80 per share is payable on March 28, 2025 to shareholders of record on March 14, 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text: check capital-return policy versus disclosure of material weaknesses and SEC investigation
rfm_tuples.M_value: Board approved a dividend INCREASE (from $3.00 to $3.20 per share annualized) in February 2025, the SAME month management presumably knew the FY2024 audit would produce an adverse ICFR opinion (the audit was running late — NT 10-K filed two weeks later). Dividend record date (March 14) is THREE days after the 10-K filing (March 11). Quarterly $0.80 dividend pay date is March 28 — sandwiched between 10-K filing and Benacin's $2.9M insider sale.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Dividend hikes and active capital returns are a common Mode-B obfuscation pattern: an explicit signal of confidence delivered concurrent with the worst disclosure year in the company's history. The choreography (dividend hike Feb, NT 10-K early March, 10-K March 11, dividend record March 14, insider sale March 21) is suspicious enough to deserve documentation even if any one piece is innocent.

rfm_tuples.R: In April 2023, our Board of Directors approved an amendment to the Coordinating and Supervising Service Agreement ('Service Agreement') that amended the fee arrangement Jean Madar Holding SAS ... The aggregate increase in fees payable to Jean Madar Holding SAS is from $1.23 million to $2.0 million on an annual basis, effective as of January 1, 2023 ... The same $2.0 million fee was paid to Jean Madar Holding SAS under the Service Agreement during 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text: check related-party governance and overlap with founder-CEO compensation
rfm_tuples.M_value: CEO/Chairman Jean Madar receives compensation routed through his personally-owned Jean Madar Holding SAS at $2.0M/year (a 63% increase from $1.23M), characterized as 'base salary' for disclosure purposes. This is the same Jean Madar Holding SAS that is the related party. The company also acknowledges that France-based ITEU 'reports to' Benacin, who is also a Director — the same officer who executed the post-10-K insider sale. No independent control over the IT general controls weakness area at the SA subsidiary.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The related-party Service Agreement plus the founder-controlled French subsidiary with the IT-general-controls material weakness create a governance environment where the people responsible for the controls also benefit personally from related-party fees. Not by itself a red flag (it has been disclosed for years), but a material contextual factor that compounds the other findings.

rfm_tuples.R: Lacoste, our newest brand for European based operations, exceeded the Company's expectations in its first year, achieving $85 million in net sales in 2024 ... Roberto Cavalli, our newest brand for United States based operations, achieved net sales of $31 million in its first year under the Company's management. ... net sales in 2024 increased 10% compared to 2023, ... of which 9% is related to new brands.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text: verify implied organic growth excluding Lacoste/Roberto Cavalli additions
rfm_tuples.M_value: Reported 2024 net sales growth: +10%, of which the 10-K explicitly states 9 percentage points came from NEW brands (Lacoste $85M, Roberto Cavalli $31M = ~$116M of new-brand revenue out of ~$1.5B+ topline). Implied organic growth ex new brands = approximately 1%. Largest legacy brand Jimmy Choo grew +7%, but Montblanc (#2) and Coach (#3) were flat/'broadly flat'. Without the two new licenses (which carry minimum advertising spend and royalty commitments), 2024 was essentially a no-growth year.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Not a falsification — the 10-K honestly discloses the 9-of-10 percentage points came from new brands. But the disclosure exists in MD&A while the headline narrative emphasizes '+10% growth.' Combined with rising customer concentration and material weaknesses in the European operations, the underlying organic growth picture is weaker than the headline.

summary: IPAR looks 'boring' on the surface (consumer staples, prestige fragrance, dividend-paying, $1.5B+ revenue with mid-single-digit organic growth) but the FY2024 10-K is a forensic-disclosure outlier. In a single filing IPAR disclosed for the first time in 20 years: (1) three material weaknesses including IT general controls at the European subsidiary responsible for ~65% of revenue, (2) an SEC informal investigation that concerns August 2023 proxy disclosures and has been live for at least a year without prior disclosure, and (3) a late 10-K (NT 10-K filed 2025-03-03). The new auditor's first attestation was adverse on ICFR. Ten days after the 10-K, the operating President of the French subsidiary executed a $2.93M discretionary open-market sale (not 10b5-1), the largest single insider transaction in over a year. The disclosures were paired with a dividend INCREASE the same month, an obfuscation pattern. Reported +10% revenue growth is 9 percentage points from two newly-licensed brands; legacy organic growth is ~1%. The R/f/M scoring framework identifies this as a high-severity 'lying detector' name despite the boring-staple optics.
